Author: B.V. Nagarathna
Bench: B.V. Nagarathna
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Crl.) No.227/2023
 Ruchi Petitioner(s)
 Versus
 Varun Dutta & Ors. Respondent(s)
 O R D E R

This Transfer Petition is filed by the petitioner/wife, seeking the following reliefs:
a) Transfer of trial of the Case No.144/2022 CNR Number HPUN04-006015-2022 titled Ruchi vs. Varun Dutta & Ors. pending before Civil Judge  cum  JMFC TC Amb, District Una, Himachal Pradesh to competent court District Court Ghaziabad at Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

entities.text: JMFC TC Amb, District Una, Himachal Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: b) pass any other order or instructions as this Honble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case and in the interest of justice.
During the pendency of this petition, the matter was referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.

Learned counsel for the respective parties submitted that the parties have arrived at a mediated settlement inasmuch as the parties do not wish to continue their marriage and seek dissolution of their marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
The terms of settlement have been been filed Reason: by the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.
Contd..
- 2 - Learned counsel for the respective parties further submitted that pursuant to the Settlement Agreement, an application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India has been filed.

Therefore,
the Settlement Agreement may be taken on record and the marriage between the parties may be dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent.
The parties are present in the Court.

They have Ruchi vs Varun Dutta on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77113883/
1 been identified by their respective counsel.

When queried by this Court, the parties submitted that they have indeed arrived at a settlement and have decided to part ways and seek dissolution of their marriage by a decree of divorce by mutual consent, as per the terms of Agreement.
They further stated that they would abide by the terms of settlement and the said settlement has been arrived on their own free will and without any coercion or undue influence from any side.

Learned counsel for the respondent submitted that totally a sum of Rs.7,00,000/- has to be paid by the respondent to the petitioner in full and final claims of the petitioner vis-a-vis her maintenance as well as permanent alimony.
A sum of Rs.3,00,000/- has already been paid by Demand Draft and a further sum of Rs.4,00,000/- is being paid today before the Court.

Learned counsel for the contd..
- 3 - petitioner has accepted the said demand draft and the receipt of the same is also acknowledged by the petitioner herein.
Learned counsel for the respective parties further drew our attention to the fact that the parties have agreed for closure of the proceedings that have been imitated by them.

The said proceedings have been referred to in paragraph 4 of the joint application filed under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, which are detailed as under - I. FIR No.027/2022 dated 08.09.2022 under Section 354, 498A, 406, 506, 34 of Indian Penal Code registered at PS : Women Police Station  UNA, District, UNA, Himachal Pradesh wherein chargesheet has been filed and Cr. Case No.144/2022 is pending before the Civil Judge  cum- JMFC, Amb, District UNA, Himachal Pradesh.
II. Application under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act 2005 bearing Matrimonial Case No.
1469/2023 which is pending before the Ld. ACJM, District Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.

Application under Section 125 of the Maintenance Case No.810/2023, which is pending in the Family Court, District Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh. IV. FIR No.12/2023 dated 08.01.2023 under Section 504, 506, IPC at wave City Police Station, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh initiated by the brother of petitioner against respondents.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In view of the Settlement and decision taken by the parties, the aforesaid proceedings are stand closed and in fact are quashed.

We have perused the terms of the Settlement Agreement as well as the joint application filed under Article 142 of the contd..
- 4 - Constitution of India.

Although, there is no matrimonial proceedings, as such, pending between the parties, they have drew a mediated settlement, decided to part ways and seek a decree of divorce by mutual consent and hence an application under Article 142 of the Constitution of India has been Ruchi vs Varun Dutta on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77113883/
2 filed jointly by them.
We have taken the same on record and perused it.
On perusal of the terms of the Settlement as well as the joint application, we find that the said terms are lawful and there is no impediment in law to accept the same.

In the circumstances, invoking our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India, the marriage between the parties, which took place on 30.07.2021 at Jourbar, District Una, Himachal Pradesh is dissolved by mutual consent.
The terms of settlement shall be read as part and parcel of this order.
Consequently, the Transfer Petition stands disposed of.
